.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 304 AM EDT Friday...

1. Dry through Saturday, then showers will impact our area on 
Sunday especially our southern zones. 

2. High pressure will provide our region with mostly dry 
conditions and below normal temperatures, along with the 
potential for frost in climo favored areas.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 304 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Dry and cool weather is expected today through 
Saturday night as a ridge of surface high pressure brushes by to
our north. Winds will be gusty out of the north northwest today
up to around 25 mph at times. Temperatures will also be cool 
enough overnight for some pockets of patchy frost in the coolest
spots of the Adirondacks and northeast Kingdom. Temperatures 
today and Saturday will range through the 60s with Saturday 
cooler than today. Then a warm front will lift into our forecast
area on Sunday and bring showers to our region, especially our 
southern zones. A southward shift in the models with this system
means we are now expecting between a trace and four tenths of 
an inch of rain through Monday morning. Bulk of this system will
be south of our region, and slide east and away from the area 
by Monday morning.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A Rex block type of pattern will develop next 
week to our west, which will hold a ridge of high pressure over 
northern New England and Quebec such that we'll get refills of 
cool and dry air. The closed upper level low that gradually 
works its way eastward through the Great Lakes region may open 
up and get pushed ever so slightly northward as it moves to the 
east, opening the door for increasing rain chances by Thursday. 

Aside from this potential rain, the only other weather of note 
will be chilly nights that set the stage for frost development. 
For now, based on the expected position of high pressure, there 
is a slightly higher chance of some patchy frost in portions of 
the Adirondacks and central/northeastern Vermont Wednesday 
morning, but it is on the table each morning Tuesday through 
Thursday with relatively light winds each night.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 06Z Saturday...Currently a wide range in flight 
conditions present ranging from VFR to LIFR which will continue 
through 12Z. A slow trend towards improving conditions is 
expected as winds off the deck increase and drying from above 
gradually erodes the low stratus and fog that is widespread at 
this hour. The northwesterly flow could more effectively mix out
the lowest clouds at sites such as EFK and MPV, while blocked 
flow helps maintain IFR conditions at BTV and RUT. Highest 
confidence in LIFR conditions throughout the next six hours 
exists at SLK, and mainly VFR conditions at PBG. Around or soon 
after 12Z, northwest winds will ramp up with gusts by 16Z in the
15 to 25 knot range at all terminals. These gusty winds will 
persist through at least 00Z at most sites before diminishing. 
Skies will be mainly clear with perhaps patchy fog development 
towards the very end of the TAF period in the vicinity of SLK 
and MPV.
